newsitem.title: UK: IPE May Brent ends up on Iran and U.S. gasoline.
newsitem.headline: IPE May Brent ends up on Iran and U.S. gasoline.

text.p: IPE May Brent crude oil ended the day firmer but off the highs. The prompt contract closed on Monday up some 29 cents at $18.17 a barrel, off the intra-day high of $18.30.

Brokers said the move upwards was triggered in part by a report in Sunday's Washington post that U.S. and Saudi intelligence authorities have linked a senior Iranian government official to a group of Shiite Moslems suspected of bombing a U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia last year.
A rally on NYMEX unleaded gasoline ahead of the U.S. driving season was also supportive and the U.S. products ended the day sharply firmer.
'It was an extremely boring day led by gasoline and the Iran story. This closing level is supportive and we may see a further move to the upside tomorrow,' one broker said.
But he warned that a build in U.S. gasoline stocks in this week's stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API) could trigger a move back down.
'If the API's are not supportive on the gasoline the whole complex could come tumbling off again,' he said.
The prompt May IPE gas oil contract, which closed earlier up $1.50 at $165 a tonne, was called to open unchanged on Tuesday.
'There is strong resistance at the $165 level and we may see gas oil falling back. There is limited buying interest in Europe,' another broker commented.
